SeasonResult: St. Andrew's defeated Greenwood Christian 2-0 at Porter-Gaud to win the SCISA Class AA boys soccer championship and finish 12-4.
StatusNote: NewsBank recovery includes the three scored SCISA Class AA playoff wins plus 13 regular-season record-path placeholders needed to reconcile the published 12-4 final record. Points for/against reflect recovered scored games only.
HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2000 boys soccer archive now restores Jim Brown's final St. Andrew's season as another championship year. The full regular-season schedule has not surfaced, but the state quarterfinal report listed St. Andrew's at 10-4 after beating Jefferson Davis Academy, and the state final report gives the final record as 12-4.

One regular-season note is clear from the title preview: Toni Popovic had scored eight goals in five matches before breaking his left arm during a win over James Island Christian. The roster and statistics preserve that official snapshot while the schedule carries a placeholder for the unscored James Island win.

The postseason run was decisive. St. Andrew's beat Jefferson Davis Academy 5-1 in the quarterfinals behind two goals each from Frank Krynen and Chris Lowe, then came from a 1-0 halftime deficit to beat James Island Christian 4-1 in the semifinals as Lee Stubbs scored twice.

In the championship match at Porter-Gaud, Evan Aldrich scored in the third minute and a Scott Thornton header forced a Greenwood Christian own goal for the 2-0 final. Cam Aldrich made 15 saves, and Will Helmken, Matt Mahany, and Chris Lowe anchored the shutout as St. Andrew's won its third SCISA boys soccer title in four years.
HighlightNotes: SCISA Class AA state champion with a 12-4 final record.
Cam Aldrich made 15 saves in the state championship shutout.
Lee Stubbs scored twice in the state semifinal win over James Island Christian.
Toni Popovic was listed with eight goals in five matches before his regular-season injury.
Justin Dixon, Quint Dixon, and Lee Stubbs were listed as St. Andrew's Ashley Dearing Award candidates in April 2000.

HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2001 boys soccer archive shows St. Andrew's making another SCISA Class AA semifinal run one year after its 2000 title. A March player-of-the-week listing credited Cam Aldrich with four goals, Fred Krynen with four goals and three assists, and Toni Popovic with five goals against Patrick Henry, confirming an early win before the first full box score surfaced.

The first recovered full result was a 5-1 win over Sea Island Academy on March 22, followed by a 4-1 win over Hilton Head Prep. After a 5-2 loss to James Island Christian and one missing loss, the Saints beat Sea Island 2-1 and Byrnes Academy 8-0, then lost a penalty-kick match to Hilton Head Prep.

St. Andrew's closed the recovered regular season with an 11-0 win over Patrick Henry and a 13-0 win over Jefferson Davis Academy. A missing win remains between the Jefferson Davis match and the state quarterfinal record line.

In the SCISA Class AA playoffs, St. Andrew's beat Calhoun Academy 5-1 to reach the semifinals with a chance at a fourth title in five years. Byrnes Academy ended the run 3-2 on penalty kicks after overtime.
HighlightNotes: Toni Popovic had at least 14 goals in recovered reports, including five in the early Patrick Henry win and a hat trick against Byrnes Academy.
Quint Dixon scored twice in the state quarterfinal win over Calhoun Academy.
Cam Aldrich was credited with at least 25 saves in recovered reports and also scored four goals in the early Patrick Henry win.
Cam Aldrich, Davy Clay, Justin Dixon, Chris Lowe, and Jeff Smith were listed as St. Andrew's Ashley Dearing Award candidates in April 2001.

HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's opened the recovered Spring 2002 boys soccer archive unbeaten. The Saints were 3-0 after a 2-1 win over Harvest Baptist, with Quint Dixon and Jacob Rauers scoring and Will Massey assisting twice.

Omar Glenn scored four goals in a 7-0 win over Jefferson Davis Academy that moved St. Andrew's to 4-0. The first recovered loss came three days later, a 4-2 result against James Island Christian despite goals from Massey and Glenn.

The record path then goes quiet until the state tournament. Published playoff coverage listed St. Andrew's at 9-7-1 after a 4-1 quarterfinal win over James F. Byrnes Academy, requiring four additional wins, six losses, and one tie between the March 21 James Island Christian result and that May 14 quarterfinal.

Hilton Head Christian had beaten St. Andrew's twice by one goal during the regular season and ended the Saints' postseason with a 5-1 semifinal win. Jacob Rauers scored the lone St. Andrew's goal in the semifinal.
HighlightNotes: Omar Glenn scored four goals against Jefferson Davis Academy and finished with five goals in recovered reports.
Will Massey had two assists against Harvest Baptist and scored against James Island Christian.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's defeated James Island Christian 4-1 at Porter-Gaud to win the SCISA Class AA boys soccer championship and finish 15-1.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. NewsBank confirms the 15-1 final record, 80-8 scoring margin entering the state final, and 84-9 final scoring margin. HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's restored the boys soccer championship standard in Spring 2003, going 15-1 and winning the SCISA Class AA title under Mark Gibbons. The recovered NewsBank results begin with a 15-0 win over Jefferson Davis Academy and continue through region wins over Harvest Baptist, James Island Christian, Patrick Henry, Hilton Head Prep, and Cathedral Academy.

The Saints' only loss came at James Island Christian on April 4, a 3-2 double-overtime result that split the regular-season series. Published record lines show three additional wins between that 3-1 record and the Apr. 30 Patrick Henry win that moved St. Andrew's to 7-1, so the schedule now carries three late-April placeholders in that gap.

An early-May broad-search result also surfaced a 6-0 win at Patrick Henry in Estill, with Beau Hinton scoring three goals and Jacob Rauers scoring twice. One more early-May placeholder is needed before the May 9 Harvest Baptist win, which listed St. Andrew's at 11-1.

The state tournament run was decisive. St. Andrew's beat The King's Academy 10-1 in the quarterfinals, edged Harvest Baptist 2-1 in the semifinal, and defeated James Island Christian 4-1 in the championship match at Porter-Gaud. Jacob Rauers scored a hat trick in the final after moving from midfield to forward, while Lyle McKenzie added the opening goal.

The championship was St. Andrew's fourth SCISA boys soccer title in six seasons, joining the 1998, 1999, and 2000 teams. The preview before the final listed Lyle McKenzie with 17 goals and 9 assists, Beau Hinton with 15 goals and 3 assists, Omar Glenn with 12 goals and 6 assists, and Jacob Rauers with 7 goals and 10 assists before Rauers' title-game hat trick.
HighlightNotes: SCISA Class AA state champion with a 15-1 final record.
SCISA Region 1 champion and top seed for the state tournament.
St. Andrew's outscored opponents 84-9, including 80-8 before the state final.
Jacob Rauers scored three goals in the championship win over James Island Christian.
Lyle McKenzie, Beau Hinton, Omar Glenn, and Jacob Rauers were the leading scorers in the recovered season record.

HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2005 boys soccer archive now begins with St. Andrew's 3-2 penalty-kick win over Cathedral Academy on April 4. Hamish Huntley scored twice, Kevin Crouch, Ryan Kirby, and Chris Rauers had assists, and Emmett Eason made six saves.

St. Andrew's then dropped non-region games to Pinewood Prep, Beaufort Academy, Beaufort Academy again, Pinewood Prep, and Hilton Head Prep. Huntley scored at Hilton Head Prep, and Ben Harrison scored against Pinewood Prep on a Huntley assist.

The Saints closed region play with a 2-1 win over Cathedral Academy on May 6. Chris Rauers and Brian Crouch scored, Kevin Crouch assisted, and Emmett Eason made six saves as St. Andrew's moved to 2-0 in SCISA Region 1-AA and earned the region's top state-tournament seed.

The May 12 Savannah Morning News listed St. Andrew's at 3-6 after a 2-0 SCISA Class AA state tournament loss to Byrnes Academy. One win remains unidentified in the recovered schedule, so the game list includes a placeholder until that score is found.
